articles.title: Local governments take charge of flood relief after criticism of centralised response
articles.summary: Amid criticism of the central government's reliance on security agencies for flood relief, local authorities in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts have taken charge. Six‑party committees have been established in each district to coordinate the distribution of aid and resources, aiming to improve efficiency and address community needs. The shift reflects growing pressure on the central administration to decentralise disaster response and empower local bodies.

articles.title: After days of managing flood victims, Bharatpur Hospital returns to treating patients
articles.summary: Bharatpur Hospital in Chitwan, Nepal, has cleared its morgue after recovering and burying 321 flood victims, with 199 bodies interred over two days. The rapid effort eased the pressure on the facility’s mortuary, allowing it to resume normal patient care and outpatient services that had been suspended during the disaster response. Hospital officials praised the coordination among staff and local authorities, emphasizing the importance of restoring healthcare services for the community after the recent flooding.

articles.title: China and India should do more to save the Himalaya system
articles.summary: The article discusses the need for China and India to take climate action to save the Himalaya system.

articles.title: The case for transparency in Nepal flood rescue flights
articles.summary: The article argues for greater transparency in the use of rescue helicopters during Nepal's recent floods, highlighting how the destruction of road networks made air transport essential for evacuations and aid. It criticizes the allocation of these limited resources to politicians and media crews, questioning the criteria for flight prioritization and calling for clear guidelines to ensure that rescue operations serve those in need first. The piece urges government accountability and public oversight to prevent misuse of emergency assets in future disasters.

articles.title: Prioritise psychological support for those affected by the Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: The article urges the Nepalese government and aid agencies to expand counselling services beyond the districts most devastated by the Bhotekoshi flood, ensuring that displaced residents and those who have returned to their home areas also receive psychological support. It highlights the long‑term mental health impacts of the disaster and calls for coordinated efforts among health officials, NGOs, and community groups to provide accessible, culturally appropriate counselling for all affected populations.

articles.title: Nepal steps up diplomatic push for support after floods
articles.summary: Following devastating floods, Nepal has intensified diplomatic efforts to secure international assistance, seeking climate recovery funds, tunnel rescue teams, forensic expertise, and essential equipment to aid reconstruction and disaster response.

articles.title: UN Women estimates 43,000 women and girls in Nepal need urgent flood assistance
articles.summary: UN Women estimates that 43,000 women and girls in Nepal require urgent assistance following recent floods, with a total of 157,050 women and girls in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot directly or indirectly affected. The humanitarian response highlights critical needs for food, safe drinking water, and protection services. UN Women calls for immediate relief efforts to address these vulnerabilities and prevent further deterioration of the situation for the affected female population.

articles.title: 1.6 million affected by Bhotekoshi floods, says government report
articles.summary: The Nepalese government’s first situation report on the Bhotekoshi River floods states that about 1.6 million people have been affected. The disaster has resulted in at least 1,050 confirmed deaths and nearly 4,000 individuals remain missing. Over 21,000 security personnel are involved in rescue and relief operations, working alongside international teams. The flooding has caused extensive damage to infrastructure, displaced thousands, and triggered a massive coordinated response across the affected regions.

articles.title: Drones take on a new role in Nepal’s disaster response—from delivering food to carrying bodies
articles.summary: The article discusses how Nepal has expanded the use of drones beyond their initial deployment by international rescue teams after the 2015 earthquake. Today, drones are employed to deliver food and medical supplies, assist in searching for survivors, and even transport bodies from inaccessible disaster zones, enhancing the country's overall emergency response capabilities.

articles.title: Authorities scramble for alternatives after Krishnabhir road cave-in
articles.summary: A major section of the Krishnabhir road has collapsed into the Trishuli River, with a 70‑metre stretch falling completely and another 120‑metre segment severely cracked. Local authorities are urgently seeking alternative routes and solutions to restore connectivity and ensure safety for commuters. The incident has disrupted transport in the region and raised concerns over the stability of nearby infrastructure.

articles.title: Family performs funeral rites after Bhotekoshi flood victim’s body goes missing
articles.summary: Relatives of Raj Kumar Shrestha performed funeral rites after his body, presumed recovered from the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood, went missing. The family said a body resembling Shrestha was photographed, but later they were told it had been transferred to TU Teaching Hospital from Nuwakot, and they could not locate it. The incident highlights ongoing distress for flood victims and their families.

articles.title: Trade shifts to under-resourced Korala point after Rasuwa and Tatopani closures
articles.summary: Following the closure of the Rasuwa and Tatopani border crossings, traders are rerouting stranded containers to the under‑resourced Korala point in upper Mustang. Nepal Customs officials have warned that the sudden shift is straining the limited manpower and equipment at Korala, prompting calls for additional resources to handle the increased trade flow and avoid bottlenecks.

articles.title: In Thecho, Matayaa becomes a festival of remembrance and satire
articles.summary: Thecho’s annual Matayaa festival this year blended remembrance with satire, honoring those who perished in the Bhotekoshi floods while continuing its tradition of using music, performance and humor to comment on societal issues. The procession highlighted the community’s resilience and offered a platform for reflection through artistic expression.

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 1,127 as 4,858 remain missing
articles.summary: The death toll from the August 26 flash flood in Nepal has risen to 1,127, with 4,858 people still missing. Search and rescue teams continue to recover bodies and look for survivors along the affected river valleys. The disaster has caused widespread devastation across several districts, prompting emergency response efforts and calls for increased aid and support for the affected communities.

articles.title: US launches new strikes on Iran and Tehran hits back in widening conflict
articles.summary: The United States carried out new airstrikes targeting Iranian military installations, prompting Tehran to launch retaliatory attacks across the Gulf region. The escalating exchanges have heightened concerns about a wider war and the potential for renewed disruptions to global oil supplies, affecting markets and regional stability.

articles.title: Rescue teams struggle to reach workers trapped in underground powerhouses
articles.summary: Rescue teams are facing severe difficulties reaching dozens of workers believed to be trapped inside underground hydropower plants after the Bhotekoshi River flood devastated the area. Thick mud and debris have blocked access routes, hampering rescue efforts. Families of the workers are demanding answers and urgent action from authorities. The incident highlights the vulnerability of Nepal's expanding hydropower infrastructure to extreme weather events and raises concerns about safety protocols and emergency preparedness.

articles.title: Sonu Sood arrives in Nepal with relief supplies for flood victims
articles.summary: Indian actor Sonu Sood arrived in Nepal with the Sood Charity Foundation to deliver food, blankets and other relief supplies to communities affected by recent floods. The actor emphasized that the foundation will continue to provide assistance over the coming months, aiming to support flood victims in the hardest‑hit areas.

articles.title: Bhotekoshi survivors reunited with families after five days
articles.summary: Twenty-three workers from Bardiya who were caught in the Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa have been rescued and reunited with their families after five days stranded in the disaster zone. The survivors returned home on Sunday, marking the end of a tense period for the affected families and highlighting ongoing rescue efforts in the region.

articles.title: PM Shah addresses five queries over government’s handling of Bhotekoshi floods
articles.summary: Prime Minister Shah faced five parliamentary questions about the government's handling of the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods. He defended the response, addressing criticism regarding the adequacy of early warnings, the management of deceased bodies, the role of foreign assistance, the execution of tunnel rescue operations, and the coordination between federal, provincial and local authorities. Shah asserted that the government acted promptly and cooperatively, while acknowledging challenges and outlining steps taken to improve disaster management.

articles.title: Nepal’s political parties call for unity as criticism grows over flood rescue
articles.summary: In the House of Representatives, leaders from Nepal's major political parties urged a coordinated response to the Bhotekoshi flood disaster, emphasizing national unity. Opposition lawmakers criticized the government's delayed rescue efforts in the tunnel, highlighting concerns over preparedness and response speed. The debate underscored growing public frustration over the handling of the catastrophe and called for improved disaster management mechanisms.

articles.title: US pounds Iran, Tehran strikes back at bases in biggest exchange since July
articles.summary: The United States intensified its military campaign against Iran, launching strikes that prompted Tehran to retaliate with attacks on U.S. bases, marking the largest exchange of fire since July. Washington warned of further, more devastating strikes, while Iran accused the U.S. of bombing a wedding party, resulting in five deaths and dozens of injuries. The escalating tit‑for‑tat raises concerns of a broader conflict in the region.

articles.title: 147 local representatives, government staff, teachers and security personnel missing after Bhotekoshi floods
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi River to flood, leaving 147 local representatives, government staff, teachers and security personnel unaccounted for. Among the missing are 83 security personnel and 64 local officials and government employees. The disaster has raised the total number of people whose whereabouts are unknown to 3,916 across the affected region. Authorities are conducting rescue and search operations while assessing the damage and coordinating relief efforts.

articles.title: Oft-battered Langtang Valley cut off after Rasuwa floods
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi River to flood in Rasuwa district, washing away the roads and bridges that connect Langtang Valley with Dhunche. With the main access routes destroyed, tourists are now reliant on helicopter transport, and authorities warn of supply shortages and uncertainty for the upcoming trekking season. The incident highlights the vulnerability of the popular trekking region to extreme weather events.

articles.title: In Bhotekoshi’s wake, experts and activists question environmental cost of AI
articles.summary: As Nepal explores establishing its own AI data centres, experts and environmental activists warn that the country must first evaluate the energy, water and broader ecological impacts of such facilities. Citing the recent Bhotekoshi river incident, they argue that unchecked development could exacerbate resource strain and pollution. The discussion highlights the need for comprehensive assessments and sustainable planning before proceeding with large‑scale digital infrastructure.

articles.title: Bhotekoshi floods halt Nepal’s electricity exports to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River has disrupted Nepal's hydroelectric output, cutting the country's electricity exports to Bangladesh from about 1,000 MW to roughly 650 MW during the wet season. The reduction threatens revenue for Nepal's power sector and may affect Bangladesh's energy supply, prompting officials from both nations to assess mitigation measures and explore alternative arrangements.
